critique: The required title, grid, Cub start token, star goal, and Run/Reset controls are present, and the board is the central object, but the puzzle state is not immediately legible: the tiny tokens and nearly uniform cream-and-green tiles make start, goal, and traversable connector topology compete at the same low contrast. The flanking story and challenge cards support the storybook tone yet consume width without helping play, while the dense route lines visually muddy the warm illustrated system. The trade-off is to preserve the authored storybook framing without letting decoration or uniform styling weaken functional reading.
suggestion: Keep the header, footer controls, board dimensions, and warm parchment identity, but enlarge the board modestly and simplify the two side cards into quieter, narrower supporting notes. Make Cub and the star unmistakable with larger bespoke illustrated markers, strong silhouettes, and one controlled warm accent reserved for active endpoints. Clarify connector paths by reducing line weight and tile texture, increasing separation between valid paths and tile backgrounds, and grouping the legend directly beneath the board. Preserve the restrained palette and handcrafted borders, then align the board, legend, and Run/Reset controls on one vertical axis so the eye reads title, objective, puzzle, then action.
audit_note: Independent FUSED review of only the task brief and common r0 screenshot; no axis critiques or later outputs were consulted.
